drug_class: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Combination (LAG-3 and PD-1 blocker)
purpose: This medicine is used to treat a type of skin cancer called melanoma that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery. It is used in adults and children 12 years and older. The goal is to help stop or slow the growth of cancer cells.
how_it_works: Your immune system has natural 'brakes' that sometimes prevent it from fighting cancer effectively. This medication works by releasing two of those brakes at the same time — one called PD-1 and another called LAG-3 — so your immune system can recognize and attack cancer cells more powerfully. Think of it like taking the handcuffs off your immune system so it can do its job better.
common_side_effects: Feeling very tired, joint or muscle pain, rash or itchy skin, nausea, diarrhea, decreased appetite, headache, and abnormal lab results. Many patients notice these side effects, but they can often be managed with your care team's help.
warnings: This medicine can cause your immune system to overreact and attack healthy organs — including your lungs, liver, intestines, kidneys, heart, or hormone glands. These can be serious or even life-threatening. Contact your doctor right away if you notice new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, severe diarrhea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, unusual fatigue, or any other new concerning symptoms. This medicine should not be used during pregnancy as it can harm an unborn baby, and you should use birth control during treatment and for a period afterward.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an IV infusion (a drip into your vein) by a healthcare professional, usually every 4 weeks. Each infusion takes about 30 minutes. Your doctor will decide how many treatment cycles you need based on how your cancer is responding and how well you are tolerating the medication.
